content: Stomatology is a specialized field of medicine recognized within the European Union, focusing on the diagnosis, treatment, and prevention of diseases and conditions affecting the mouth and its associated structures. It requires a minimum of three years of postgraduate university training beyond a medical degree (MD) and is often integrated into dental education. The specialty is defined under the European Medical Directive 2001/19/EC. The study and practice of stomatology encompass a wide range of procedures and treatments, including the following: Diseases of the Periodontium (Parodentium) 1. Removal of Dental Deposits: Supragingival and subgingival deposits are removed using manual techniques or ultrasonic devices like the Piezon Master. 2. Oral Hygiene Education: Patients are instructed on proper oral hygiene practices to maintain periodontal health. 3. Hygiene Monitoring: 4. Medical Treatment of Gingival and Periodontal Canals: Therapeutic interventions are performed to address infections or inflammation. 5. Flap Surgery: Surgical procedures are carried out to treat advanced periodontal disease. 6. Application of Medical-Protective Dressings: Protective bandages are applied post-treatment to aid healing. 7. Selective Tooth Filing: Adjustments are made to the occlusal surfaces of teeth to improve function or alleviate discomfort. 8. Temporary Splinting: Teeth are stabilized using temporary splints in cases of mobility or trauma. Diseases of the Oral Mucosa 1. Collection of Diagnostic Samples: Samples are taken from the oral cavity for: Cytological analysis Virological analysis Bacterioscopic analysis 2. Irrigation with Medicinal Agents: Therapeutic irrigation is performed using: Anesthetics Anti-infective agents Enzymatic preparations Keratoplasty agents 3. Administration of Injections: Injections are administered for: Delivery of pharmaceutical compositions Nerve blockades Preventive or initial treatment of teeth with anti-caries agents 4. Preparation and Restoration of Carious Cavities: Carious lesions are prepared and restored using various techniques: Treatment of Pulpitis: Management of inflamed pulp includes: Pulp devitalization Preservation of viable pulp tissue Use of endodontic handpieces for precision Removal of coronal and root pulp Determination of the working length of root canals 6.
